style_spec:
PYTHON MODULE STYLE CONTRACT — every generated or revised module must satisfy all of these:
1. Every public function and method has a complete type-annotated signature (parameter types and return type) and a Google-style docstring (Args/Returns/Raises — only the sections that apply).
2. Every module defines __all__ listing exactly its public names, in the order they are defined.
3. Imports are grouped stdlib, then third-party, then local, each group alphabetized internally and separated from the next by exactly one blank line; no wildcard imports.
4. Plain data holders are @dataclass, not a hand-rolled __init__ that just assigns attributes.
5. Custom exceptions subclass a single module-level base exception documented with a one-line docstring; never raise a bare Exception.
6. No bare `except:` — every except names the exception type(s) it catches.
7. No print() for diagnostics — a module-level `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` is used instead.
8. Lines wrap at 100 columns, four-space indentation, no trailing whitespace.
9. Standard PEP 8 casing: PascalCase classes, snake_case functions/methods/variables, UPPER_SNAKE_CASE module-level constants.
